prompt:
You are helping a security test lab design a test for one published weakness. The lab can only run tests built from the building blocks listed below. You choose from them; you cannot add code, commands or new cases. If no building block can show this weakness, say so: an honest "no test" is a good answer, and a test that cannot catch the weakness is a bad one.

Advisory: CVE-2024-42461 (other names: GHSA-49q7-c7j4-3p7m)
Package: elliptic (npm)
Published: 2024-08-02

The lab's reading of the advisory (already checked against the publisher's text):

{
  "affected": {
    "quote": {
      "source": "S1",
      "text": "\"last_known_affected_version_range\": \"<= 6.5.6\""
    },
    "versions": "introduced in 5.2.1; last known affected version range <= 6.5.6 (that is, 5.2.1 up to and including 6.5.6)"
  },
  "area": "ecdsa_signature_check",
  "fixed": {
    "quote": {
      "source": "S1",
      "text": "\"fixed\": \"6.5.7\""
    },
    "version": "6.5.7"
  },
  "kind": "accepts_bad_signature",
  "notes": "The signature wrongly accepted here is one whose bytes are not written in the strict format; the sources do not say that a signature is accepted for a message that was never signed. The advisory's sentence names only version 6.5.6, but the record's range starts earlier, on a separate S1 line: \"introduced\": \"5.2.1\". In the code excerpts the one difference is that getLength in 6.5.7 (S2) returns false when a length spread over extra bytes starts with a 0x00 byte; 6.5.6 (S3) has no such check and reads a length padded with a leading zero byte whenever its value is above 0x7f. The excerpts show only this one function, so any other changes in 6.5.7 are not shown here.",
  "plain_name": "Loosely encoded signature accepted",
  "weakness": "When it reads an ECDSA signature, the affected elliptic accepts signatures written in the looser BER format, not only the strict DER format. As a result the same signature can be rewritten as different bytes and still be accepted, which the advisory calls signature malleability.",
  "weakness_quote": {
    "source": "S1",
    "text": "In the Elliptic package 6.5.6 for Node.js, ECDSA signature malleability occurs because BER-encoded signatures are allowed."
  }
}

The one building block: "signature_cases" (Published signature cases)
- What it does: Hands the program published ECDSA P-256 signatures (Project Wycheproof, pinned by SHA-256), one at a time, and compares its accept or reject with the published right answer.
- What it fits: A program or library that checks ECDSA P-256 signatures over SHA-256, in DER form.
- Its control: "accept_all_verifier". A deliberately broken checker that accepts every signature. It must get every must-reject case wrong, so the selection needs at least one must-reject case.
- Its pass rule: Passed only if every answer is right. Any wrong answer means Failed.
- It cannot test: timing or other side channels; signing (only checking); any other curve, hash or signature scheme; a crash that the program turns into a plain rejection.

The published cases it can run come from Project Wycheproof, file ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256_test.json (484 cases). The file groups its cases by kind (a "flag"). For each kind: how many cases, how many must be rejected or accepted, and the file's own published note.
